discovery: Proposal and realisation of electron and nuclear spin qubits in semiconductors

nominees.name: Bruce E. Kane
nominees.affiliation: Laboratory for Physical Sciences, University of Maryland, USA

nominees.name: Lieven M. K. Vandersypen
nominees.affiliation: QuTech and Delft University of Technology, Netherlands

subfield: Condensed matter physics / quantum information (semiconductor spin qubits)
motivation: Loss (with DiVincenzo, 1998) showed that single electron spins confined in semiconductor quantum dots could serve as qubits, with exchange-coupled two-qubit gates. Kane's 1998 proposal to encode quantum information in the spins of individual phosphorus donors in isotopically pure silicon created a new field of atomic-scale silicon quantum devices. Vandersypen turned these ideas into reality: single-shot spin readout, coherent single-spin control by electric fields, and high-fidelity two-qubit gates and small processors in silicon and germanium. Together, these contributions established that quantum coherence of single spins can be engineered and controlled inside the same material platform as classical microelectronics. Semiconductor spin qubits now achieve gate fidelities above fault-tolerance thresholds and are made in industrial foundries. This offers a credible path to scalable quantum computation. It complements the 2025 prize for superconducting circuits.
